title: Man who died in shootout with police was violating day parole
article: The man who died in a shootout with Ontario Provincial Police on Sunday was being sought for violating day parole while serving a lengthy prison sentence for trying to kill a Montreal police officer in 1991.

Daniel Lamer, 37, was killed in a shootout with Const. Dan Brisson, 28, after a car was pulled over on Highway 401 near Cornwall for a traffic violation. Brisson suffered wounds to the back of his head and back and was expected to recover.
Lamer, of Montreal, had a record for violent crime and was released on parole almost nine years after taking a Montreal police officer hostage and nearly killing him.
Law-enforcement officials said Tuesday that they were upset to learn of Lamer's criminal record.
